scenes.text: You'd think the grid's toughest hour is the hottest afternoon. In sunny states, it's often sunset.
Take demand, subtract wind and solar, and California's curve sags at midday, then shoots up at night. It's called the duck curve.
Batteries help. In 2025, California's grid operator reported batteries delivered about 9,100 megawatts on average in the hour ending at 8 p.m. In 2024, it was about 5,700.
They charge on cheap midday sun and run after dark. The full video is on Other End of the Wire.
